name: graphify
description: "Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content â€” especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. ---

# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```
/graphify                                             # full pipeline on current directory (HTML viz; add --obsidian for a vault)
/graphify <path>                                      # full pipeline on specific path
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>           # clone repo then run full pipeline on it
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --branch <branch>  # clone a specific branch
/graphify <url1> <url2> ...                           # clone multiple repos, build each, merge into one cross-repo graph
/graphify <path> --mode deep                          # thorough extraction, richer INFERRED edges
/graphify <path> --update                             # incremental - re-extract only new/changed files
/graphify <path> --directed                            # build directed graph (preserves edge direction: sourceâ†’target)
/graphify <path> --whisper-model medium                # use a larger Whisper model for better transcription accuracy
/graphify <path> --cluster-only                       # rerun clustering on existing graph
/graphify <path> --no-viz                             # skip visualization, just report + JSON
/graphify <path> --html                               # (HTML is generated by default - this flag is a no-op)
/graphify <path> --svg                                # also export graph.svg (embeds in Notion, GitHub)
/graphify <path> --graphml                            # export graph.graphml (Gephi, yEd)
/graphify <path> --neo4j                              # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for Neo4j
/graphify <path> --neo4j-push bolt://localhost:7687   # push directly to Neo4j
/graphify <path> --falkordb                           # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --falkordb-push falkordb://localhost:6379   # push directly to FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --mcp                                # start MCP stdio server for agent access
/graphify <path> --watch                              # watch folder, auto-rebuild on code changes (no LLM needed)
/graphify <path> --wiki                               # build agent-crawlable wiki (index.md + one article per community)
/graphify <path> --obsidian --obsidian-dir ~/vaults/my-project  # write vault to custom path (e.g. existing vault)
/graphify add <url>                                   # fetch URL, save to ./raw, update graph
/graphify add <url> --author "Name"                   # tag who wrote it
/graphify add <url> --contributor "Name"              # tag who added it to the corpus
/graphify query "<question>"                          # BFS traversal - broad context
/graphify query "<question>" --dfs                    # DFS - trace a specific path
/graphify query "<question>" --budget 1500            # cap answer at N tokens
/graphify path "AuthModule" "Database"                # shortest path between two concepts
/graphify explain "SwinTransformer"                   # plain-language explanation of a node
```

## What graphify is for

Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

## What You Must Do When Invoked

If the user invoked `/graphify --help` or `/graphify -h` (with no other arguments), print the contents of the `## Usage` section above verbatim and stop. Do not run any commands, do not detect files, do not default the path to `.`. Just print the Usage block and return.

**Fast path â€” existing graph:** Before doing anything else, check whether `graphify-out/graph.json` exists. The expected location is `graphify-out/graph.json` relative to the **current working directory** (i.e. the project root where you are running commands). If it exists AND the user's request is a natural-language question about the codebase (e.g. "How does X work?", "What calls Y?", "Trace the data flow through Z") and NOT an explicit rebuild command (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, or a bare path/URL that implies fresh extraction): **skip Steps 1â€“5 entirely and jump straight to `## For /graphify query`.** Run `graphify query "<question>"` immediately. Do not run detect. Do not check corpus size. Do not ask the user to narrow. The graph is already built â€” use it.

If no path was given, use `.` (current directory). Do not ask the user for a path.

If the path argument starts with `https://github.com/` or `http://github.com/`, treat it as a GitHub URL - run Step 0 before anything else, then continue with the resolved local path.

Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps.

### Step 0 - GitHub repos and multi-path merge (only if a URL or several paths)

Only when the path is one or more `https://github.com/...` URLs, or several local subfolders to merge. See `references/github-and-merge.md` for the clone, cross-repo merge, and monorepo flow, then continue with the resolved local path. A plain local path skips this step.

### Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed

```powershell
# Detect Python with graphify â€” uv/pipx-aware (fixes #831)
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path graphify-out | Out-Null
$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON = $null

function Find-GraphifyPython {
    # 1. uv tool install â€” 'uv tool dir' is authoritative, respects UV_TOOL_DIR automatically
    if (Get-Command uv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $uvDir = (uv tool dir 2>$null).Trim()
        if ($uvDir) {
            $py = Join-Path $uvDir "graphifyy\Scripts\python.exe"
            if (Test-Path $py) {
                & $py -c "import graphify" 2>$null
                if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return $py }
            }
        }
    }
    # 2. pipx install â€” 'pipx environment' respects PIPX_HOME automatically
    if (Get-Command pipx -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $venvs = (pipx environment --value PIPX_LOCAL_VENVS 2>$null).Trim()
        if ($venvs) {
            $py = Join-Path $venvs "graphifyy\Scripts\python.exe"
            if (Test-Path $py) {
                & $py -c "import graphify" 2>$null
                if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return $py }
            }
        }
    }
    # 3. Active venv / conda / pip-into-current-env
    $pyCmd = Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($pyCmd) {
        & $pyCmd.Source -c "import graphify" 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            return (& $pyCmd.Source -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)").Trim()
        }
    }
    return $null
}

# Try to find the right Python (uv â†’ pipx â†’ active env)
$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON = Find-GraphifyPython

# Not found â€” install then re-detect
if (-not $GRAPHIFY_PYTHON) {
    if (Get-Command uv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3
    } else {
        pip install graphifyy -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3
    }
    $GRAPHIFY_PYTHON = Find-GraphifyPython
}

# Save interpreter path â€” all subsequent steps read this.
# `Out-File -Encoding utf8` always writes a BOM on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (utf8NoBOM
# only exists from PowerShell 6), and that BOM rides into the saved path, so the hook
# rebuild fails with WinError 123 (#3028). WriteAllText with an explicit BOM-less
# encoding writes the bytes POSIX writes, and adds no trailing newline.
$Utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $PWD 'graphify-out\.graphify_python'), [string]$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON, $Utf8NoBom)
# Save scan root so `graphify update` (no args) knows where to look next time
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $PWD 'graphify-out\.graphify_root'), (Resolve-Path INPUT_PATH).Path, $Utf8NoBom)
```

If the import succeeds, print nothing and move straight to Step 2.

**In every subsequent block, run Python through the saved interpreter â€” `& (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python)` in place of a bare `python3` â€” so every step uses the interpreter that actually has graphify.**

### Step 2 - Detect files

```powershell
@'
import json
from graphify.detect import detect
from pathlib import Path
result = detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))
# Write the sidecar from Python, not a shell redirect, so the same block renders
# on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528).
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
print(f'Detected {result["total_files"]} files')
'@ | & (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python) -
```

Replace INPUT_PATH with the actual path the user provided. Do NOT cat or print the JSON - read it silently and present a clean summary instead:

```
Corpus: X files Â· ~Y words
  code:     N files (.py .ts .go ...)
  docs:     N files (.md .txt ...)
  papers:   N files (.pdf ...)
  images:   N files
  video:    N files (.mp4 .mp3 ...)
```

Omit any category with 0 files from the summary.

Then act on it:
- If `total_files` is 0: stop with "No supported files found in [path]."
- If `skipped_sensitive` is non-empty: report the count and list the skipped file names, so a wrongly-flagged source or doc is visible and can be renamed or moved (#2106).
- If `total_words` > 2,000,000 OR `total_files` > 500: show the warning. Then compute the top 5 first-level subdirectories by file count:
  - Read `scan_root` from the detect JSON (always an absolute path to the resolved INPUT_PATH).
  - Concatenate all file lists across all types (`code`, `document`, `paper`, `image`, `video`).
  - Filter out any path that starts with `scan_root + "/graphify-out/"` to exclude converted sidecars.
  - For each file, strip the `scan_root` prefix and take the first path component. Files directly in `scan_root` with no subdirectory count as `(root)`.
  - If all files are in `(root)` with no subdirectories, do not ask to narrow â€” no subfolders exist. Instead suggest `--no-cluster` to skip the expensive clustering step and proceed.
  - Otherwise rank by count, show the top 5 with file counts, then ask which subfolder to run on. Wait for the user's answer before proceeding.
- Otherwise: proceed directly to Step 2.5 if video files were detected, or Step 3 if not.

### Step 2.5 - Video and audio (only if video files detected)

Skip this step entirely if `detect` returned zero `video` files. When the corpus has video or audio, see `references/transcribe.md` to transcribe them to text first, then treat the transcripts as doc files in Step 3.

### Step 3 - Extract entities and relationships

**Before starting:** note whether `--mode deep` was given. You must pass `DEEP_MODE=true` to every subagent in Step B2 if it was. Track this from the original invocation - do not lose it.

This step has two parts: **structural extraction** (deterministic, free) and **semantic extraction** (LLM, costs tokens).

> **graphify needs no API key. Never ask the user for one, and never block on one.** Code is extracted structurally (AST) with no LLM and no key at all â€” a code-only corpus (the common `/graphify .` on a repo) skips semantic extraction entirely, so it needs nothing here: go straight to Part A and skip Part B. Semantic extraction (only for docs, papers, and images) uses Gemini **only if** `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` is already set; otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM. graphify does **not** read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or any other provider key. If you catch yourself about to prompt for, wait on, or stop because of a missing API key, that is a misread of this skill â€” proceed without one.

**Before semantic extraction:** check whether `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is set. If neither is set, print this one-liner to the user:
> Tip: set `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` to use Gemini for semantic extraction (`pip install 'graphifyy[gemini]'`).

Print it once, then continue â€” do not wait for the user to supply a key. If `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` IS set, use `graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel(files, backend="gemini")` for semantic extraction instead of dispatching subagents. The default Gemini model is `gemini-3-flash-preview`; set `GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL` or pass `--model` in headless CLI flows to override it.

> **No other API keys are read.** When `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` are unset, semantic extraction falls to the host agent itself â€” the running session is the LLM. On a host that dispatches subagents (e.g. Codex), dispatch them as written in Part B. On a host that runs the CLI directly in a terminal and cannot dispatch subagents, do not stall: a code-only corpus has no semantic work, so write the empty semantic file (Part B "Fast path") and continue to Part C; for a corpus with docs/papers/images, either set a Gemini key or extract those inline yourself, but in no case prompt for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` â€” that prompt is a misread of this skill.

**Run Part A (AST) and Part B (semantic) in parallel. Dispatch all semantic subagents AND start AST extraction in the same message. Both can run simultaneously since they operate on different file types. Merge results in Part C as before.**

Note: Parallelizing AST + semantic saves 5-15s on large corpora. AST is deterministic and fast; start it while subagents are processing docs/papers.

#### Part A - Structural extraction for code files

For any code files detected, run AST extraction in parallel with Part B subagents:

```powershell
@'
import sys, json
from graphify.extract import collect_files, extract
from pathlib import Path
import json

code_files = []
detect = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
for f in detect.get('files', {}).get('code', []):
    code_files.extend(collect_files(Path(f)) if Path(f).is_dir() else [Path(f)])

if code_files:
    result = extract(code_files, cache_root=Path('INPUT_PATH'))
    Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f'AST: {len(result["nodes"])} nodes, {len(result["edges"])} edges')
else:
    Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').write_text(json.dumps({'nodes':[],'edges':[],'input_tokens':0,'output_tokens':0}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print('No code files - skipping AST extraction')
'@ | & (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python) -
```

#### Part B - Semantic extraction (parallel subagents)

**Fast path:** If detection found zero docs, papers, and images (code-only corpus), skip Part B entirely and go straight to Part C. AST handles code - there is nothing for semantic subagents to do. **First write an empty semantic file** so Part C's merge has its input (it reads `.graphify_semantic.json` unconditionally; without this a code-only run hits `FileNotFoundError`):

```powershell
@'
import json
from pathlib import Path
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').write_text(json.dumps({'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[],'input_tokens':0,'output_tokens':0}), encoding='utf-8')
'@ | & (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python) -
```

**MANDATORY: You MUST use the Agent tool here. Reading files yourself one-by-one is forbidden - it is 5-10x slower. If you do not use the Agent tool you are doing this wrong.**

Before dispatching subagents, print a timing estimate:
- Load `total_words` and file counts from `graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json`
- Estimate agents needed: `ceil(uncached_non_code_files / 22)` (chunk size is 20-25)
- Estimate time: ~45s per agent batch (they run in parallel, so total â‰ˆ 45s Ã— ceil(agents/parallel_limit))
- Print: "Semantic extraction: ~N files â†’ X agents, estimated ~Ys"

**Step B0 - Check extraction cache first**

Before dispatching any subagents, check which files already have cached extraction results:

SPEC_PATH below is the **absolute** path of the `references/extraction-spec.md` that ships beside this SKILL.md â€” the same file Step B2 loads and hands to every subagent. It is the extraction prompt, so cache entries are attributed to it: when a graphify upgrade changes the prompt, entries produced by the old one are re-extracted instead of replayed, and unchanged prompts keep their entries (#1939). Substitute the real path in both Step B0 and Step B3 â€” pass the same one to each, and do not drop the argument.

```powershell
@'
import json
from graphify.cache import check_semantic_cache
from pathlib import Path

detect = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
# Only content files go to semantic extraction. Code is already covered structurally
# by the AST pass (Part A); flattening every category here makes subagents re-read
# every source file (#1392). Video is transcribed to a document in Step 2.5 first.
all_files = [f for cat in ('document', 'paper', 'image') for f in detect['files'].get(cat, [])]

cached_nodes, cached_edges, cached_hyperedges, uncached = check_semantic_cache(all_files, root='INPUT_PATH', prompt_file='SPEC_PATH')

# Always (re)write the cache file: write hits, else DELETE any leftover from a prior
# run so Part C never merges a stale .graphify_cached.json (#1392).
if cached_nodes or cached_edges or cached_hyperedges:
    Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').write_text(json.dumps({'nodes': cached_nodes, 'edges': cached_edges, 'hyperedges': cached_hyperedges}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
else:
    Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').unlink(missing_ok=True)
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt').write_text('\n'.join(uncached), encoding="utf-8")
print(f'Cache: {len(all_files)-len(uncached)} files hit, {len(uncached)} files need extraction')
'@ | & (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python) -
```

Only dispatch subagents for files listed in `graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt`. If all files are cached, skip to Part C directly.

**Step B1 - Split into chunks**

Load files from `graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt`. Split into chunks of 20-25 files each. Each image gets its own chunk (vision needs separate context). When splitting, group files from the same directory together so related artifacts land in the same chunk and cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted.

**Step B2 - Dispatch ALL subagents in a single message**

Call the Agent tool multiple times IN THE SAME RESPONSE - one call per chunk. This is the only way they run in parallel. If you make one Agent call, wait, then make another, you are doing it sequentially and defeating the purpose.

**IMPORTANT - subagent type:** Always use `subagent_type="general-purpose"`. Do NOT use `Explore` - it is read-only and cannot write chunk files to disk, which silently drops extraction results. General-purpose has Write and Bash access which the subagent needs.

Concrete example for 3 chunks:
```
[Agent tool call 1: files 1-15, subagent_type="general-purpose"]
[Agent tool call 2: files 16-30, subagent_type="general-purpose"]
[Agent tool call 3: files 31-45, subagent_type="general-purpose"]
```
All three in one message. Not three separate messages.

Each subagent receives this exact prompt (substitute FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE, and CHUNK_PATH).

CHUNK_PATH must be an **absolute** path â€” derive it before dispatching:
```powershell
$PROJECT_ROOT = (Get-Location).Path  # cwd â€” where Part C globs graphify-out\ (NOT .graphify_root/scan dir, #1392)
# Then for chunk N: $CHUNK_PATH = Join-Path $PROJECT_ROOT "graphify-out\.graphify_chunk_0N.json"
```

Subagent prompt template:

See `references/extraction-spec.md` for the exact subagent prompt (JSON schema, node-ID rules, confidence rubric, frontmatter, hyperedge, and vision rules). Load it only here, only when at least one chunk holds a doc, paper, or image; a pure-code corpus has skipped Part B and never reads it. Pass each subagent that prompt verbatim with FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE, and CHUNK_PATH substituted, and have it write the result to CHUNK_PATH.

**Step B3 - Collect, cache, and merge**

Wait for all subagents. For each result:
- Check that `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json` exists on disk â€” this is the success signal
- If the file exists and contains valid JSON with `nodes` and `edges`, include it and save to cache
- If the file is missing, the subagent was likely dispatched as read-only (Explore type) â€” print a warning: "chunk N missing from disk â€” subagent may have been read-only. Re-run with general-purpose agent." Do not silently skip.
- If a subagent failed or returned invalid JSON, print a warning and skip that chunk - do not abort

If more than half the chunks failed or are missing, stop and tell the user to re-run and ensure `subagent_type="general-purpose"` is used.

Merge all chunk files into `.graphify_semantic_new.json`. **After each Agent call completes, read the real token counts from the Agent tool result's `usage` field and write them back into the chunk JSON before merging** â€” the chunk JSON itself always has placeholder zeros. Then run:
```powershell
@'
import json, glob
from pathlib import Path

chunks = sorted(glob.glob('graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json'))
all_nodes, all_edges, all_hyperedges = [], [], []
total_in, total_out = 0, 0
for c in chunks:
    d = json.loads(Path(c).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    all_nodes += d.get('nodes', [])
    all_edges += d.get('edges', [])
    all_hyperedges += d.get('hyperedges', [])
    total_in += d.get('input_tokens', 0)
    total_out += d.get('output_tokens', 0)
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').write_text(json.dumps({
    'nodes': all_nodes, 'edges': all_edges, 'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,
    'input_tokens': total_in, 'output_tokens': total_out,
}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
print(f'Merged {len(chunks)} chunks: {total_in:,} in / {total_out:,} out tokens')
'@ | & (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python) -
```

Save new results to cache. Pass the same SPEC_PATH as Step B0 â€” it stamps each entry with the prompt that produced it, and a write under a different prompt than the read lands where the next run won't look (#1939):
```powershell
@'
import json
from graphify.cache import save_semantic_cache
from pathlib import Path

new = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}
uncached = [line for line in Path('graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt').read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line]
saved = save_semantic_cache(new.get('nodes', []), new.get('edges', []), new.get('hyperedges', []), root='INPUT_PATH', allowed_source_files=uncached, prompt_file='SPEC_PATH')
print(f'Cached {saved} files')
'@ | & (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python) -
```

Merge cached + new results into `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json`:
```powershell
@'
import json
from pathlib import Path

cached = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}
new = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}

all_nodes = cached['nodes'] + new.get('nodes', [])
all_edges = cached['edges'] + new.get('edges', [])
all_hyperedges = cached.get('hyperedges', []) + new.get('hyperedges', [])
seen = set()
deduped = []
for n in all_nodes:
    if n['id'] not in seen:
        seen.add(n['id'])
        deduped.append(n)

merged = {
    'nodes': deduped,
    'edges': all_edges,
    'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,
    'input_tokens': new.get('input_tokens', 0),
    'output_tokens': new.get('output_tokens', 0),
}
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
print(f'Extraction complete - {len(deduped)} nodes, {len(all_edges)} edges ({len(cached["nodes"])} from cache, {len(new.get("nodes",[]))} new)')
'@ | & (Get-Content graphify-out\.graphify_python) -
```
Clean up temp files: `Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue graphify-out\.graphify_cached.json, graphify-out\.graphify_uncached.txt, graphify-out\.graphify_semantic_new.json`

#### Part C - Merge AST + semantic into final extraction

```powershell
@'
import sys, json
from pathlib import Path

ast = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
sem = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

# Merge: AST nodes first, semantic nodes deduplicated by id
seen = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}
merged_nodes = list(ast['nodes'])
for n in sem['nodes']:
    if n['id'] not in seen:
        merged_nodes.append(n)
        seen.add(n['id'])

merged_edges = ast['edges'] + sem['edges']
merged_hyperedges = sem.get('hyperedges', [])
merged = {
    'nodes': merged_nodes,
    'edges': merged_edges,
    'hyperedges': merged_hyperedges,
    'input_tokens': sem.get('input_tokens', 0),
    'output_tokens': sem.get('output_tokens', 0),
}
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
total = len(merged_nodes)
```

```powershell
extract = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
# In --update mode, 'all_files' carries the full corpus; 'files' is the changed
# subset. Full-rebuild mode populates only 'files', so the fallback handles that.
# root= relativizes the manifest keys to the scan root (same base as the build),
# so the on-disk manifest is portable across clones/machines and a later --update
# matches cached files instead of missing every one (#1417).
#
# Only stamp semantic files (docs/papers/images) that ACTUALLY produced output:
# a detected file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the
# next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost
# forever (#2015). This mirrors the library extract path exactly
# (cli._stamped_manifest_files + clear_semantic + scan_corpus); do not stamp the
# raw corpus. Code files are always stamped (AST is deterministic); only semantic
# types are gated on output.
from graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files

_manifest_files = _stamped_manifest_files(_corpus, extract, Path('INPUT_PATH'))
# Files dispatched this run (the changed subset) but NOT stamped above still carry
# a stale semantic_hash from a prior run; clear it so detect_incremental re-queues
# them instead of reading them as unchanged (#1948).
_sem_types = ('document', 'paper', 'image')
_dispatched = {f for t, fl in detect['files'].items() if t in _sem_types for f in fl}
_stamped = {f for fl in _manifest_files.values() for f in fl}
_cleared = _dispatched - _stamped
# scan_corpus = the RAW full corpus (not the stamp-filtered subset) so in-root
# files newly excluded since last run are dropped rather than masquerading as
# deletions; untouched files' prior rows are still preserved (#1908).
_scan = {f for fl in _corpus.values() for f in fl}
save_manifest(_manifest_files, root='INPUT_PATH', scan_corpus=_scan, clear_semantic=_cleared or None)

input_tok = extract.get('input_tokens', 0)
output_tok = extract.get('output_tokens', 0)

    'input_tokens': input_tok,
    'output_tokens': output_tok,
    'files': detect.get('total_files', 0),

cost['total_output_tokens'] += output_tok
cost_path.write_text(json.dumps(cost, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

print(f'This run: {input_tok:,} input tokens, {output_tok:,} output tokens')
print(f'All time: {cost["total_input_tokens"]:,} input, {cost["total_output_tokens"]:,} output ({len(cost["runs"])} runs)')
```

"""Phase 2D: persisted, evidence-backed executor qualification for the client-side composition (schema v2).

A qualification record says: THIS client (client_id + its Ed25519 public key) qualified THIS provider, run as THIS
launch chain (executable file + every pinned file the launcher executes, each with SHA-256) at THIS reported version,
for THESE models, at THIS level, on the strength of THIS evidence file, until THIS expiry. It lives in the client's own
state root (`<client_root>/control/supervisor/qualification/<provider>.json`, evidence under `.../qualification/evidence/`)
and is re-validated on every load:

  * signature: Ed25519 by the client's own key over the canonical record (independent review round 1, D1/D3: an
    unkeyed digest could be recomputed after editing `models`; an unbound record could be copied to another client);
  * binding: `client_id` and `client_public_key` must equal the composing client's manifest values;
  * expiry: `expires_at` (epoch seconds) must lie in the future;
  * evidence: the client-owned evidence file must still hash to `evidence_sha256` AND its content must agree with the
    record (provider, success, version, executable hash) (review D2: the evidence was never re-read);
  * launch chain: the executable and every `pinned_files` entry must still hash as recorded, and every `resolve_pins`
    name (for example `node` for the npm shim) must still resolve, on the executor PATH, to the pinned file (review D4:
    only the `.cmd` shim was pinned, not the program it launches);
  * `--version` must still report the recorded version; `FIXTURE_ONLY` only when the composition allows fixtures.

Anything that fails leaves the provider where the frozen Phase 1 registry leaves it by default: `NATIVE_UNQUALIFIED`,
not usable. Authentication is never persisted: it is probed live on every registry decision (`codex login status`,
`claude auth status`) under the executor's environment allow-list, never by reading a credential file or logging in.

Trust limit (stated, not hidden): the signing key is the client key protected by current-user DPAPI (Phase 1 C1:
same-user logical isolation only). A process running as the same Windows user can sign. The record defends against
hand edits, copies between clients, stale evidence and launcher/payload replacement, not against same-user malware.

class QualificationError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, code, detail=None):
        super().__init__(code if detail is None else f"{code}: {detail}")

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RecordTrust:
    """The composing client's identity: records must be bound to it and signed by its key."""
    client_id: str
    public_key_hex: str

    @staticmethod
    def from_manifest(data: dict) -> "RecordTrust":

def _public_hex(key: Ed25519PrivateKey) -> str:
    return key.public_key().public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw).hex()


def qualification_dir(client_root) -> Path:

def _canonical(record: dict) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({k: v for k, v in record.items() if k not in ("record_sha256", "signature")}, sort_keys=True,
                      separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True).encode("utf-8")


def record_digest(record: dict) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(_canonical(record)).hexdigest()


# ---- launch chain discovery --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def executor_path(environ=None) -> str:
    """The PATH the supervisor forwards to executors (same allow-list as `ExecutorSpec.build_env`)."""
    env = environ if environ is not None else os.environ
    return env.get("PATH", "")


def npm_codex_launch_chain(shim, environ=None):
    """For the npm `codex.cmd` launcher: every file the launch executes or loads by name, and the `node` resolution.
    Returns (pinned_files {abs path: sha256}, resolve_pins {name: abs path}). Raises QualificationError if the chain
    cannot be established (unknown layout = no native qualification)."""
    shim = Path(shim).resolve()
    dp0 = shim.parent
    pinned, resolve = {}, {}
    local_node = dp0 / "node.exe"
    if local_node.is_file():
        node = local_node.resolve()
    else:
        found = shutil.which("node", path=executor_path(environ))
        if not found:
            raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_NODE_UNRESOLVED")
        node = Path(found).resolve()
        resolve["node"] = str(node)
    pkg = dp0 / "node_modules" / "@openai" / "codex"
    entry = pkg / "bin" / "codex.js"
    if not entry.is_file():
        raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_ENTRY_MISSING")
    platform_pkg = pkg / "node_modules" / "@openai" / "codex-win32-x64"
    vendor = platform_pkg / "vendor" / "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"
    if not (vendor / "bin" / "codex.exe").is_file():
        raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_VENDOR_MISSING")
    files = [node, entry, pkg / "package.json", platform_pkg / "package.json"]
    files += sorted(p for p in vendor.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in (".exe", ".dll", ".js", ".cmd", ".ps1"))
    for f in files:
        pinned[str(Path(f).resolve())] = _file_sha256(f)
    return pinned, resolve


def launch_chain_for(spec_id, executable, environ=None):
    if spec_id == "codex_cli" and Path(executable).suffix.lower() == ".cmd":
        return npm_codex_launch_chain(executable, environ)
    if Path(executable).suffix.lower() in (".cmd", ".bat", ".ps1"):
        raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_UNKNOWN_LAUNCHER", Path(executable).name)
    return {}, {}

def build_record(*, client_root, client_id, signer: Ed25519PrivateKey, provider, level, spec_id, executable,
                 executable_args, version, models, evidence_path, qualified_by, notes=None, pinned_files=None,
                 resolve_pins=None, ttl_s=DEFAULT_TTL_S, now=None) -> dict:
    """Build and sign a record from observed facts. The caller is the trusted qualification run of THIS client. The
    evidence file is copied into the client's own qualification store (content-addressed) and hashed there."""
    if not isinstance(provider, str) or not _PROVIDER.fullmatch(provider):
        raise QualificationError("PROVIDER_ID_INVALID")
    if level not in LEVELS:
        raise QualificationError("LEVEL_INVALID", str(level))
    if spec_id not in BUILTIN_SPECS:
        raise QualificationError("SPEC_UNKNOWN", str(spec_id))
    if not isinstance(client_id, str) or not _UUID.fullmatch(client_id):
        raise QualificationError("CLIENT_ID_INVALID")
    exe = Path(executable)
    if not exe.is_file():
        raise QualificationError("EXECUTABLE_MISSING")
    args = [str(a) for a in (executable_args or [])]
    ev = Path(evidence_path)
    if not ev.is_file():
        raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_MISSING")
    if not isinstance(models, (list, tuple)) or not models:
        raise QualificationError("MODELS_REQUIRED")
    for m in models:
        if m is not None and (not isinstance(m, str) or not _MODEL.fullmatch(m)):
            raise QualificationError("MODEL_ID_INVALID", str(m))
    if version is not None and not isinstance(version, str):
        raise QualificationError("VERSION_INVALID")
    if not isinstance(ttl_s, int) or not 60 <= ttl_s <= MAX_TTL_S:
        raise QualificationError("TTL_INVALID")
    if pinned_files is None and resolve_pins is None:
        pinned_files, resolve_pins = launch_chain_for(spec_id, exe)
    data = ev.read_bytes()
    ev_sha = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    ev_name = f"{provider}-{ev_sha[:16]}.json"
    d = evidence_dir(client_root)
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (d / ev_name).write_bytes(data)
    now = int(time.time() if now is None else now)
    record = {"schema": SCHEMA, "provider": provider, "level": level, "spec_id": spec_id, "client_id": client_id,
              "client_public_key": _public_hex(signer), "executable": str(exe.resolve()), "executable_args": args,
              "executable_sha256": _file_sha256(exe), "pinned_files": dict(sorted((pinned_files or {}).items())),
              "resolve_pins": dict(sorted((resolve_pins or {}).items())), "version": version, "models": list(models),
              "evidence_file": ev_name, "evidence_sha256": ev_sha, "qualified_at": now, "expires_at": now + ttl_s,
              "qualified_by": str(qualified_by), "notes": notes or ""}
    record["record_sha256"] = record_digest(record)
    record["signature"] = signer.sign(_canonical(record)).hex()
    return record

    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = d / (record["provider"] + ".json")
    tmp = path.with_name(path.name + "." + uuid.uuid4().hex + ".tmp")
    with open(tmp, "x", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(record, f, indent=1, sort_keys=True)
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    os.replace(tmp, path)
    return path


def validate_shape(record) -> dict:
    if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record) - set(REQUIRED) - set(OPTIONAL) or any(k not in record for k in REQUIRED):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA")
    if record["schema"] != SCHEMA:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "schema")
    if not isinstance(record["provider"], str) or not _PROVIDER.fullmatch(record["provider"]):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "provider")
    if record["level"] not in LEVELS:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "level")
    if record["spec_id"] not in BUILTIN_SPECS:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "spec_id")
    if not isinstance(record["client_id"], str) or not _UUID.fullmatch(record["client_id"]):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "client_id")
    if not isinstance(record["client_public_key"], str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", record["client_public_key"]):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "client_public_key")
    if not isinstance(record["executable"], str) or not record["executable"]:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "executable")
    if not isinstance(record["executable_args"], list) or any(not isinstance(a, str) for a in record["executable_args"]):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "executable_args")
    pf = record["pinned_files"]
    if not isinstance(pf, dict) or any(not isinstance(k, str) or not isinstance(v, str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(v) for k, v in pf.items()):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "pinned_files")
    rp = record["resolve_pins"]
    if not isinstance(rp, dict) or any(not isinstance(k, str) or not _RESOLVE_NAME.fullmatch(k) or not isinstance(v, str) or v not in pf
                                       for k, v in rp.items()):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "resolve_pins")
    for key in ("executable_sha256", "evidence_sha256", "record_sha256"):
        if not isinstance(record[key], str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(record[key]):
            raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", key)
    if not isinstance(record["evidence_file"], str) or not _EVIDENCE_NAME.fullmatch(record["evidence_file"]):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "evidence_file")
    for key in ("qualified_at", "expires_at"):
        if type(record[key]) is not int:
            raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", key)
    if not 0 < record["expires_at"] - record["qualified_at"] <= MAX_TTL_S:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "ttl")
    if record["version"] is not None and not isinstance(record["version"], str):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "version")
    models = record["models"]
    if not isinstance(models, list) or not models or any(m is not None and (not isinstance(m, str) or not _MODEL.fullmatch(m)) for m in models):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "models")
    if not isinstance(record["signature"], str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{128}", record["signature"]):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SCHEMA", "signature")
    if record_digest(record) != record["record_sha256"]:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH")
    return record


def verify_trust(record, trust: RecordTrust):
    """Binding + signature. The digest alone is recomputable by anyone; the signature is not (review D1/D3)."""
    if trust is None:
        raise QualificationError("NO_TRUST_ANCHOR")
    if record["client_id"] != trust.client_id or record["client_public_key"] != trust.public_key_hex:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_CLIENT_MISMATCH")
    try:
        Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(bytes.fromhex(trust.public_key_hex)).verify(bytes.fromhex(record["signature"]), _canonical(record))
    except (InvalidSignature, ValueError):
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_SIGNATURE_INVALID") from None


def load_records(client_root) -> list:
    """Every record file, parsed or marked unreadable. Never raises for one bad file."""
    out = []
    d = qualification_dir(client_root)
    if not d.is_dir():
        return out
    for p in sorted(d.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            rec = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            validate_shape(rec)
            if rec["provider"] != p.stem:
                raise QualificationError("RECORD_PROVIDER_FILENAME_MISMATCH")
            out.append({"path": str(p), "record": rec, "error": None})
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            code = exc.code if isinstance(exc, QualificationError) else "RECORD_UNREADABLE"
            out.append({"path": str(p), "record": None, "error": code})
    return out


def native_auth_probe(provider, executable, environ=None, timeout_s=30):
    """Live read-only authentication status. True / False / None (unknown). Never logs in, never reads a credential
    file: the CLI's own status command decides, under the same environment allow-list the executor gets."""
    argv = AUTH_STATUS_ARGV.get(provider)
    if argv is None:
        return None
    env = harness_env(AUTH_VARS.get(provider, ()), environ)
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([executable, *argv], capture_output=True, timeout=timeout_s, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, env=env)
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return None
    out = p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    err = p.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    if provider == "claude_code":
        try:
            data = json.loads(out)
            return bool(data.get("loggedIn")) if isinstance(data, dict) else None
        except ValueError:
            return None
    # Codex 0.158.0 prints "Logged in using ChatGPT" on STDERR with exit 0 (Phase 2D defect D-D1: stdout alone read as
    # "not logged in"). "Not logged in" exits non-zero. Both streams are inspected; exit status decides first.
    text = (out + chr(10) + err).lower()
    if p.returncode != 0 or "not logged in" in text:
        return False
    return "logged in" in text


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClientComposition:
    registry: HarnessRegistry
    executors: dict
    report: list          # one row per record file: provider, status (QUALIFIED | INVALIDATED), reason, level, ...
    allow_fixture: bool

    def qualified(self):
        return sorted(r["provider"] for r in self.report if r["status"] == "QUALIFIED")


def _spec_for(record) -> ExecutorSpec:
    spec = BUILTIN_SPECS[record["spec_id"]]
    if record["level"] == "FIXTURE_ONLY":
        if record["spec_id"] != GENERIC_NDJSON.executor_id:
            raise QualificationError("FIXTURE_SPEC_REQUIRED")
        return replace(GENERIC_NDJSON, executor_id=record["provider"], stdin="instructions")
    if spec.executor_id != record["provider"]:
        raise QualificationError("SPEC_PROVIDER_MISMATCH")
    return spec


def check_launch_chain(pinned_files, resolve_pins, environ=None):
    """Every pinned file still present with its hash; every resolve pin still resolves to its pinned file on the
    executor PATH. Raises QualificationError. Shared by load-time re-validation and the bridge's per-run check."""
    for path, digest in dict(pinned_files).items():
        if not Path(path).is_file():
            raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_MISSING", Path(path).name)
        if _file_sha256(path) != digest:
            raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_HASH_MISMATCH", Path(path).name)
    for name, path in dict(resolve_pins).items():
        found = shutil.which(name, path=executor_path(environ))
        if not found or _same_file(found, path) is not True:
            raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_RESOLUTION_CHANGED", name)


def _check_evidence(record, client_root):
    p = evidence_dir(client_root) / record["evidence_file"]
    if not p.is_file():
        raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_MISSING")
    data = p.read_bytes()
    if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != record["evidence_sha256"]:
        raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH")
    try:
        ev = json.loads(data)
    except ValueError:
        raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISMATCH", "not json") from None
    if not isinstance(ev, dict) or ev.get("provider") != record["provider"]:
        raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISMATCH", "provider")
    if record["level"] == "FIXTURE_ONLY":
        if ev.get("fixture") is not True:
            raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISMATCH", "fixture")
        # Fixture evidence names the models it covers; the record may not claim more (review round 2, R2-2).
        if "models" in ev and list(ev["models"]) != list(record["models"]):
            raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISMATCH", "models")
        return
    # NATIVE: the direct probe record of the qualification run must show a successful probe of this very executable,
    # at this version. The record qualifies EXACTLY the probed model, nothing more (review round 2, R2-2: a signed
    # record could list models that were never exercised).
    if ev.get("ok") is not True or ev.get("version") != record["version"] or ev.get("executable_sha256") != record["executable_sha256"]:
        raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISMATCH", "probe")
    if list(record["models"]) != [ev.get("model")]:
        raise QualificationError("EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISMATCH", "model")


def revalidate(record, *, client_root, trust: RecordTrust, allow_fixture=False, now=None, environ=None) -> tuple:
    """-> (spec, resolved executable, args) or raises QualificationError with the invalidation reason."""
    verify_trust(record, trust)
    if int(time.time() if now is None else now) >= record["expires_at"]:
        raise QualificationError("RECORD_EXPIRED")
    if record["level"] == "FIXTURE_ONLY" and not allow_fixture:
        raise QualificationError("LEVEL_NOT_ALLOWED", "FIXTURE_ONLY")
    spec = _spec_for(record)
    _check_evidence(record, client_root)
    exe = record["executable"]
    cmd = resolve_command(exe)
    if not cmd or not Path(exe).is_file() or _same_file(cmd[0], exe) is not True:
        raise QualificationError("EXECUTABLE_MISSING")
    if _file_sha256(exe) != record["executable_sha256"]:
        raise QualificationError("EXECUTABLE_HASH_MISMATCH")
    if record["level"] == "NATIVE_QUALIFIED" and Path(exe).suffix.lower() in (".cmd", ".bat", ".ps1") and not record["pinned_files"]:
        raise QualificationError("LAUNCH_CHAIN_NOT_PINNED")
    check_launch_chain(record["pinned_files"], record["resolve_pins"], environ)
    for a in record["executable_args"]:
        if Path(a).is_absolute() and Path(a).suffix == ".py" and not Path(a).is_file():
            raise QualificationError("EXECUTABLE_ARGS_MISSING")
    probe = probe_version([exe, *record["executable_args"]])
    if not probe["installed"] or probe["version"] != record["version"] or record["version"] is None:
        raise QualificationError("VERSION_MISMATCH", f"{probe.get('version')} != {record['version']}")
    return spec, exe, list(record["executable_args"])


def compose_client(client_root, *, trust: RecordTrust, allow_fixture=False, auth_probe=None, environ=None,
                   adapters_factory=None, now=None, clock=None) -> ClientComposition:
    """Phase 1 `HarnessRegistry` (all adapters, nothing qualified) plus every persisted record that re-validates now
    for THIS client (`trust`).

    `auth_probe(harness_id) -> True|False|None` defaults to the live CLI status probe for providers with a valid record
    (fixture records are authenticated by definition) and None (AUTH_UNVERIFIED) for everything else. The registry calls
    it on every `discover()`/`selectable()`, i.e. immediately before each bridge execution: nothing is cached."""
    from uri_harness_adapters import default_registry
    factory = adapters_factory or default_registry
    # `now` fixes composition time (tests); `clock` is consulted at every later re-validation (default: wall clock).
    now_fn = clock or (lambda: time.time() if now is None else now)
    rows, executables, bindings, exe_of, levels, composed = [], {}, {}, {}, {}, {}
    for item in load_records(client_root):
        rec = item["record"]
        if rec is None:
            rows.append({"provider": Path(item["path"]).stem, "status": "INVALIDATED", "reason": item["error"], "path": item["path"]})
            continue
        try:
            spec, exe, args = revalidate(rec, client_root=client_root, trust=trust, allow_fixture=allow_fixture, now=now_fn(), environ=environ)
        except QualificationError as exc:
            rows.append({"provider": rec["provider"], "status": "INVALIDATED", "reason": exc.code, "detail": exc.detail,
                         "level": rec["level"], "path": item["path"]})
            continue
        executables[rec["provider"]] = [exe, *args]
        exe_of[rec["provider"]], levels[rec["provider"]] = exe, rec["level"]
        composed[rec["provider"]] = (item["path"], rec["record_sha256"])
        bindings[rec["provider"]] = ExecutorBinding(spec=spec, resolved_executable=exe, extra_argv=tuple(args), version=rec["version"],
                                                   executable_sha256=rec["executable_sha256"], qualified_models=tuple(rec["models"]),
                                                   pinned_files=tuple(sorted(rec["pinned_files"].items())),
                                                   resolve_pins=tuple(sorted(rec["resolve_pins"].items())),
                                                   revalidate=(lambda p=rec["provider"]: still_valid(p)))
        rows.append({"provider": rec["provider"], "status": "QUALIFIED", "reason": None, "level": rec["level"], "models": list(rec["models"]),
                     "executable": exe, "executable_sha256": rec["executable_sha256"], "pinned_files": len(rec["pinned_files"]),
                     "version": rec["version"], "evidence_sha256": rec["evidence_sha256"], "qualified_at": rec["qualified_at"],
                     "expires_at": rec["expires_at"], "path": item["path"]})

    def still_valid(provider):
        """None while the record composed for `provider` still holds NOW: same record bytes on disk (no silent swap
        for another record, even a validly signed one), and a full re-validation (signature, expiry, evidence, launch
        chain, version). Otherwise the reason code. Review round 2, R2-1."""
        path, digest = composed[provider]
        try:
            rec_now = validate_shape(json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            return exc.code if isinstance(exc, QualificationError) else "RECORD_UNREADABLE"
        if rec_now["record_sha256"] != digest:
            return "RECORD_CHANGED_SINCE_COMPOSITION"
        try:
            revalidate(rec_now, client_root=client_root, trust=trust, allow_fixture=allow_fixture, now=now_fn(), environ=environ)
        except QualificationError as exc:
            return exc.code
        return None

    def probe(harness_id):
        if harness_id not in exe_of:
            return None
        if still_valid(harness_id) is not None:
            return None            # qualification no longer holds: AUTH_UNVERIFIED -> not usable (fail closed)
        if levels[harness_id] == "FIXTURE_ONLY":
            return True
        if auth_probe is not None:
            return auth_probe(harness_id)
        return native_auth_probe(harness_id, exe_of[harness_id], environ)

    registry = factory(executables, auth_probe=probe)
    for row in rows:
        if row["status"] != "QUALIFIED":
            continue
        p = row["provider"]
        if p not in registry.adapters or registry.adapters[p].refused:
            row.update(status="INVALIDATED", reason="PROVIDER_REFUSED_OR_UNKNOWN")
            bindings.pop(p, None)
            continue
        registry.qualify(p, row["level"], row["evidence_sha256"])
    return ClientComposition(registry=registry, executors=bindings, report=rows, allow_fixture=bool(allow_fixture))
"""SupervisorBridge: one verified ticket -> one durable supervisor task -> one Phase 1 receipt outcome.

Ownership: Core (frozen) owns intent, confirmation, approval, the ticket and the settlement. The supervisor
(Phase 2A) owns admission, fenced attempts, containment and reconciliation. This bridge owns only the
translation between them, and it is deliberately narrow:

  * the task id IS the ticket's operation id (canonical UUID): the same ticket can never create two tasks;
  * the authorization row is derived from the ticket (op classes, the user's explicit executor, the per-run
    workspace, validity = [issued_at, deadline)); the supervisor re-checks that scope at every admission;
  * admission is restricted to that one task (`only_task_id`), so a ticket can never run queued foreign work;
  * when the bridge returns, the task's authority is closed: a settled ticket never leaves re-admittable work;
  * on construction (= restart) every unfinished task's authority is revoked and nothing is re-launched,
    matching Phase 1 (`ExecutionJournal.recover`: claimed work becomes execution_uncertain, never a relaunch);
  * `verified` is returned only when the supervisor's ledger says COMPLETE, i.e. URI itself observed the
    required postcondition; executor claims never reach the receipt as success.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import hashlib

import os

# Same prefix the frozen client runtime / server use: "nothing effect-capable was started".
NOT_STARTED = "NOT_STARTED:"
POOL = "harness_slot"
CAPABILITY = "harness_task"
TOOL_ACTIVITY = ("tool_result", "tool_result_batch", "file_change")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExecutorBinding:
    """How one user-selectable provider is run by the supervisor. `spec.executor_id` must equal the provider id."""
    spec: ExecutorSpec
    resolved_executable: str | None = None
    extra_argv: tuple = ()
    version: str | None = None
    # Optional pin (Phase 2C): SHA-256 of the executable FILE the qualification evidence was produced with. When set,
    # the bridge hashes the resolved file before every run and refuses a different one (`EXECUTOR_BINARY_HASH_MISMATCH`).
    # Note the limit: for a launcher shim (npm `codex.CMD`) this pins the shim, not the interpreter it starts.
    executable_sha256: str | None = None
    # Optional pin (Phase 2D): the models this provider was qualified with. When set, a ticket whose bound selection
    # names another model (or none) is refused before any task exists (`MODEL_NOT_QUALIFIED`). Qualification is
    # evidence about one (provider, executable, model) triple; a different model never inherits it silently.
    qualified_models: tuple | None = None
    # Launch-chain pins (independent review round 1, D4): ((abs path, sha256), ...) every file the launcher executes,
    # and ((name, abs path), ...) names the launcher resolves on PATH (e.g. `node` for the npm `codex.cmd` shim). Both are
    # re-checked before every run; a replaced payload behind an unchanged shim is refused before any task exists.
    pinned_files: tuple = ()
    resolve_pins: tuple = ()
    # Re-validation hook (independent review round 2, R2-1): called before EVERY execution; returns None when the
    # persisted qualification (record bytes, signature, expiry, evidence, launch chain, version) still holds, else a
    # reason code. Without it a long-lived worker kept honouring a record that had expired or lost its evidence.
    revalidate: object = None


def _fit(s, n=128):
    return s if len(s) <= n else s[:n]


def _file_sha256(path):
    try:
        return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    except OSError:
        return None


def _same_file(a, b):
    """True only when both paths resolve to the same existing file (case-insensitive on Windows)."""
    try:
        ra, rb = os.path.realpath(a), os.path.realpath(b)
        if not (os.path.isfile(ra) and os.path.isfile(rb)):
            return False
        return os.path.normcase(ra) == os.path.normcase(rb) or os.path.samefile(ra, rb)
    except OSError:
        return False


class SupervisorBridge:
    def __init__(self, client_root, *, registry=None, executors: dict | None = None, clock=time.time,
                 max_attempts: int = 2, timeout_s: float = 120, inactivity_s: float = 60):
        self.root = Path(client_root).resolve()
        self.registry = registry                      # Phase 1 HarnessRegistry: install/auth/qualification gate
        self.executors = dict(executors or {})
        self.clock = clock
        self.max_attempts, self.timeout_s, self.inactivity_s = int(max_attempts), float(timeout_s), float(inactivity_s)
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        self._cancel_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._cancelled: set[str] = set()        # task ids whose caller withdrew the work (Phase 2D)
        self._running: dict[str, int] = {}       # task id -> attempt id currently supervised by this bridge
        for provider, b in self.executors.items():
            if b.spec.executor_id != provider:
                raise BridgeRefused("EXECUTOR_BINDING_ID_MISMATCH", provider)
        control = self.root / "control" / "supervisor"
        control.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.sup = Supervisor(control / "ledger.db")   # startup recovery runs here (new epoch)
        self.L = self.sup.ledger
        self.startup_report = self._revoke_unfinished_authority("RESTART")
        self._ensure_pool()
        self._ensure_registrations()

    # ---- composition ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def quota_pool(provider):
        """One breaker per provider: a quota hit on one provider never blocks the user's explicit choice of another."""
        return "quota_" + provider

    def _ensure_pool(self):
        if self.L.q1("SELECT 1 FROM resource_pool WHERE name=?", (POOL,)) is None:
            self.sup.registry.create_pool(POOL, 1, kind="harness")
        for provider in self.executors:
            if self.L.q1("SELECT 1 FROM resource_pool WHERE name=?", (self.quota_pool(provider),)) is None:
                self.sup.registry.create_pool(self.quota_pool(provider), 1, kind="quota")

    def _ensure_registrations(self):
        current = {r["executor_id"]: r for r in self.sup.registry.current_registrations()}
        for provider, b in self.executors.items():
            row = current.get(provider)
            want = json.dumps(b.spec.to_json(), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
            qp = [self.quota_pool(provider)]
            # The quota pool is also CLAIMED: Phase 2A consults breakers only on claimed pools (admission.admit_next),
            # so an open per-provider breaker must sit on a pool the attempt claims to actually block admission.
            claims = {POOL: 1, self.quota_pool(provider): 1}
            if row is not None and json.dumps(json.loads(row["spec_json"]), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) == want \
                    and json.loads(row["quota_pools_json"]) == qp and json.loads(row["claims_json"]) == claims:
                continue
            self.sup.registry.register_executor(b.spec, capabilities=[CAPABILITY], claims=claims, quota_pools=qp,
                                                version=b.version)

    def close(self):
        self.sup.close()

    # ---- restart discipline --------------------------------------------------------------
    def _revoke_unfinished_authority(self, why):
        """Every task that is not COMPLETE loses its authorization; QUEUED/RETRY_SAFE become FAILED. Nothing is
        re-launched. Returns a public report (ids and states only)."""
        out = []
        now = self.L.now_us()
        rows = self.L.q("SELECT t.task_id,t.state,t.reason_code FROM task t WHERE t.state IN ('QUEUED','RETRY_SAFE') OR EXISTS "
                        "(SELECT 1 FROM authorization a WHERE a.task_id=t.task_id AND a.superseded_at_us IS NULL "
                        "AND (a.valid_until_us IS NULL OR a.valid_until_us>?)) ORDER BY t.task_seq", (now,))
        for t in rows:
            tid, state = t["task_id"], t["state"]
            self._expire_authorization(tid)
            new_state = state
            if state in ("QUEUED", "RETRY_SAFE"):
                try:
                    self.L.transition(tid, "FAILED", "AUTHORITY_REVOKED_" + why, t["reason_code"])
                    new_state = "FAILED"
                except LedgerError:
                    new_state = self.L.task(tid)["state"]
            out.append({"task_id": tid, "was": state, "state": new_state, "authority": "revoked"})
        return out

    def _expire_authorization(self, tid):
        row = self.L.q1("SELECT scope_json FROM authorization WHERE task_id=? AND superseded_at_us IS NULL ORDER BY auth_id DESC LIMIT 1", (tid,))
        scope = json.loads(row[0]) if row else {}
        now = self.L.now_us()
        # [now, now) is empty: no admission can ever find this authorization valid again.
        self.sup.supersede_authorization(tid, scope=scope, valid_until_us=now, issued_by="uri_supervisor_bridge")

    def reconcile_restart(self):
        """Public view of what construction did: recovered decisions are in the ledger; this lists revocations."""
        return list(self.startup_report)

    # ---- execution ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def execute(self, work: AuthorizedWork):
        """-> (outcome, evidence, failure_category) in the frozen TurnRunner/ExecutionReceipt vocabulary
        ('verified' | 'failed' | 'quota' | 'execution_uncertain')."""
        with self._lock:
            return self._execute(work)

    def _execute(self, work: AuthorizedWork):
        L, tid = self.L, work.task_id
        if L.task(tid) is not None:
            # The ticket's operation already exists in the ledger: dispatch may already have happened. Never
            # a second task, never NOT_STARTED.
            return "execution_uncertain", [], "DUPLICATE_OPERATION"
        if self.registry is None:
            return "failed", [], NOT_STARTED + "NO_HARNESS_REGISTRY"

## 4. Adversarial implementation review

The Phase 2B `verify_authority` and `SupervisedTurnRunner.begin` bind signed ticket, confirmed intent, arguments, and selection. Unique operation IDs, fenced attempts, reconciliation and receipt construction address ordinary replay and duplicate local execution. The single-threaded worker validates frame shapes and preserves pending state in memory. Source and tests cover stale ticket, swapped provider/model, duplicate operation, crash and resumed session cases; the environment prevented an independent full execution of those tests (section 9).

The qualification boundary is weaker than its own stated contract. The record digest is a plain recomputable hash. `probe_qualification.py` built a valid record for `model_a`, changed it to `model_b`, recomputed `record_sha256`, and both `validate_shape` and `revalidate` accepted it. It also replaced the referenced evidence file and observed that `revalidate` still succeeded. `revalidate` never reopens or checks the evidence file or its claimed digest. `compose_client` then promotes the record into the Phase 1 registry. The candidateâ€™s own architecture acknowledges the limitation, so its `NATIVE_QUALIFIED` wording must be scoped to the shim. No real payload replacement was performed on the user's installation.

Run-scoped authentication is checked while composing the client; `SupervisorBridge.execute` uses the cached registry status and does not repeat `native_auth_probe` immediately before admission. Revocation/expiry while a worker remains alive is therefore detected only by the CLI when it runs. The test suite does not prove prompt invalidation of the displayed capability state. The approval digest is optional in the worker frame, and the frozen Flutter client sends `{turn_id, approve}` without it ([paired_runtime.dart](../../uri-agent/uri_ui/lib/services/paired_runtime.dart):177). The server ticket and pending turn still bind the approved arguments, so I did not find an argument substitution exploit from this alone. Mid-run `turn_cancel` cannot be processed while `turn_decide` is executing: [worker_service.py](../../uri-agent/uri_supervisor_bridge/worker_service.py):38-53 only cancels pending turns, and [run_uri_supervised_worker.py](../../uri-agent/scripts/run_uri_supervised_worker.py):142-184 is a serial read/handle/write loop. The bridge can cancel from a second thread, but the worker protocol has no such concurrent path. Killing the worker is coarser and may leave uncertain effects. The copy-out verifier only checks a regular nonempty file and hashes it; it does not establish that arbitrary external actions have not happened. Therefore claims of duplicate **external** side-effect prevention must be limited to the taskâ€™s declared local-write effect and executor posture, not generalized to unrestricted tool use.
